newsitem.title: UK: UK beef export plan shows promise.
newsitem.headline: UK beef export plan shows promise.

text.p: The European Union's agriculture commissioner, Franz Fischler, gave a cautious welcome on Friday to new British proposals aimed at persuading Brussels to ease its ban on British beef exports.

Britain on Tuesday committed itself to a twin-track approach to win over the EU, which imposed the ban after scientists reported evidence in March 1996 that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy, could be transmitted to humans.

As well as modifying a scheme to allow cattle from herds that have not suffered from the disease to be certified safe for export, the farm ministry said it was drawing up proposals to permit the export of animals born after a certain date.
Addressing a beef conference in Wales, Fischler said of the latter scheme: "Although the devil always tends to be in the detail, this idea seems, on the face of it, to have the merit of simplicity."
He said important progress had also been made in examining Britain's request for exports from certified herds.
EU vetinerary scientists raised objections to the scheme last month and asked Britain to clarify a number of points.
"We shall then have to see whether on a scientific level the scheme can be given a green light," Fischler, whose speech was released by the European Commission in London, said.
He said he was aware that farmers in the United Kingdom, who have been hit hard by the beef ban, felt their patience was being stretched.
"Nevertheless, all the practical aspects of a staged lifting of the ban need to be examined thoroughly by the scientific experts. This takes time," Fischler said.
